Two methods for solving this ambiguity are presented in theory and through simulation. A Radar, designed to simultaneously implement both methods, is built and the measured results are presented.

articleTitle: Synthetic aperture radar imaging with a low transmitter duty-cycle for automotive applications
abstract: In this work, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging on a 77 GHz automotive radar hardware is demonstrated. In the design of the system, the effect of low transmission duty-cycle of automotive radar chipsets is investigated. The impact of this constraint to the SAR imaging capabilities has been analysed. We propose a non-coherent summing of sub-aperture images to mitigate the effects of the low duty-cycle. An experiment was set-up on a car park scenario. Generated offline SAR images, using back-projection algorithm, show resolution of around 3° on a single channel system.

articleTitle: Sidelobe blanking with weibull fluctuation model
abstract: The performance analysis of the sidelobe blanking (SLB) system with noncoherent integration in the presence of jammer entering through sidelobes of the radar antenna is considered. The closed-form performance probabilities both in the blanking and detection regions are derived for independent but not necessary identically distributed Weibull fluctuating target and/or jammer, which are useful for configuration parameter settings of the SLB system. Finally, several numerical results of the SLB system with typical parameters are obtained and discussed.

articleTitle: Adaptive-on-transmit using information theoretic measures
abstract: The Marginal Fisher Information (MFI) metric is used to design waveforms for the sake of informationally optimal adaptiveon-transmit radar operation. A framework for MFI waveform design is introduced and Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) estimation is extended into an adaptive and dynamic sensing paradigm. The efficacy of the MFI waveform design and MMSE estimation are experimentally demonstrated. The radar transmit signal is then optimized to improve the information (i.e., reduce the estimate error variance) about a target space. The target profile is optimally updated using an iterative MMSE estimator and the signal optimization is repeated. This adaptive radar concept is shown to provide exceptional resolution and detection of even the smallest scatterers in a complex target space. These concepts maximize the information (e.g., resolution and accuracy) that can be extracted from a radar operating in a congested spectrum, where transmit signal bandwidth is potentially constrained.

articleTitle: Periodic signals detection and deinterleaving using Hidden Markov Models
abstract: The use of Hidden Markov Models for radar frequency track detection is studied in this paper. In particular, we focus on periodic signals, and propose a new algorithm that incorporates information about the periodicity in the Hidden Markov Model. Two frequency estimation methods are used, namely the Forward-Backward algorithm, and the Viterbi algorithm. The impact of including the periodicity of the signal into these algorithms is studied through simulations.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of the RCS of a small fixed-wing UAV during a typical flight
abstract: The presence and importance of of small UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) are increasing. With traditional radar detection the target RCS (Radar Cross Section) and its statistical properties are needed in order to design the detector and to assess detection performance. In this paper we make a statistical analysis of the RCS of a certain small fixed-wing UAV using measured data from a typical flight. Using data from a typical flight instead of measurements or electro-magnetic calculations as a function of aspect angle is a convenient method. Our analysis results in mean values, medians and standard deviations, in suitable Weibull probability distributions and in decorrelation times for the RCS, which are necessary for design and assessment of the detection performance.

articleTitle: Sparsity-based high-resolution analysis of mixed-mode over-the-horizon radar signals
abstract: Doppler frequency analysis is important in over-the-horizon radar (OTHR) in order to determine important target parameters such as the target altitude. In this paper, we analyze the Doppler signatures of OTHR signals propagated through both ordinary and extraordinary electromagnetic modes. As the signals following the two propagation modes undergo different group delays, the Doppler frequencies of a target associated with these two modes differ from each other. The frequency analysis of the resulting Doppler signatures becomes challenging when the Doppler components associated with these two modes are closely separated or even partially overlapping. In this paper, we develop a low-complexity sparsity-based method to resolve the Doppler signatures corresponding to the two propagation modes. It is based on a Lasso-based approach and the computational complexity is effectively reduced by employing a frequency focusing transform. To demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach, simulation results are presented for challenging scenarios where the multipath Doppler signatures corresponding to the two propagation modes are interlaced or very close to each other.

articleTitle: The non-uniform FFT (NUFFT) as an interpolator for fast clutter rendering
abstract: The non-uniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT) is a useful tool for efficiently computing a discrete Fourier transform on irregularly sampled data, or for computing an arbitrary set of frequency bins on regularly sampled data. It finds common application in radar in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) processing, and in the computation of array factor for complex antenna geometries. This paper shows how this technique can also be used as efficient interpolator when rendering ground clutter. The performance and implementation of the NUFFT will be discussed, along with its use as an interpolator. Finally, the impact of clutter rendering artefacts on adaptive processing will be demonstrated with examples from space-time adaptive processing (STAP), and how these can be mitigated through the use of the NUFFT.

articleTitle: 5G based passive radar: a feasibility study
abstract: In recent years, 5G technology has found rapid implementation in telecommunication infrastructure throughout the word. While 5G networks promise enhanced mobile telecommunication services, their capabilities for passive radar operations have yet to be fully investigated. This paper describes the passive radar principles and signal characteristics of a 5G based passive radar and provides a link budget analysis to assess its detection range. Additionally the ambiguity function characteristics of the 5G signal are examined under different configurations to assess the potential impact on the passive radar performance.

articleTitle: A novel multi-pulse repetition frequency set selection method based on the clear area evaluation matrix
abstract: Since the traditional multiple pulse repetition frequency (PRF) selection methods do not consider the influence of measurement errors and granularity division, this paper introduces a novel medium pulse repetition frequency (MPRF) set selection method for the ground-based pulsed-Doppler radar system. Specifically, we define the clear area evaluation matrix (CAEM) and derive the analytic expression of the objective function using the truth table. Compared with the traditional method based on the blind zone map (BZM), the CAEM based method preliminarily selects the measurement data considering the influence of measurement errors. To keep in line with practical processing, the CAEM solves the ambiguity of some measurement points and uses the deviation tolerance to select the results again. The genetic algorithm (GA) is utilized to maximize the objective function. The experiments show that CAEM improves computational efficiency by about 38 times and the accuracy by about 7% compared with the BZM method.

articleTitle: Study of utility of practical radon transform track-before-detect in multi-function radar
abstract: Reliable detection and tracking of targets that present a low signal-to-background ratio in radar is not trivial, but has always been an important sensor requirement, such as for detection and tracking of small boats in a maritime environment, or the detection and tracking of small unmanned air vehicles. The Radon transform has previously been considered as an approach for temporal integration of data over multiple scans. This paper describes a new practical approach to implementing a Radon transform that has a more efficient implementation than traditional methods and can operate with data from a multi-function radar where the update rates are non-uniform.

articleTitle: Cognitive CFAR parameter optimization for detection in Sea Clutter
abstract: The performance of a proposed Cognitive Radar detection method is investigated and compared again conventional CFAR detection for the case of detection of small targets in simulated Sea Clutter. The proposed method attempts to compare the local clutter statistics with the overall recent statistics and use this knowledge, coupled with existing external knowledge of CFAR performance in sea clutter, to optimally set CFAR window length. A gain in minimal SCR for a specific detection rate was observed for a range of simulated sea clutter conditions, which could then be utilized to either reduce false alarm rate for a specific detection rate, or to maintain false alarm rate and increase detection rate (as compared to a conventional detector).

articleTitle: Adaptive monopulse error estimation for radar track updates
abstract: Adaptive beamforming and monopulse processing can enable accurate estimation of target direction in environments containing jamming and clutter or other sources of interference. However, the accurate direction estimates may not translate to improved tracking performance if we have poor knowledge of the corresponding direction-errors. Incorrect direction-error estimation may lead to the tracker placing high confidence in poor quality direction estimates or vice-versa. Previous open literature publications provide an approach for estimating direction-errors for known target parameters (e.g. mean amplitude and fluctuation model). Although suited to performance comparison of different adaptive monopulse schemes, this approach leads to direction-error estimates that are not fully representative of those at the target tracker. This paper develops an approach for estimation of monopulse direction-errors for radar track updates and includes modelling results to demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Multi-static radar for manoeuvre detection
abstract: In this paper we study the benefits of using multi-static radar for manoeuvre detection in satellites. We present the conditions in which a multi-static radar is advantageous, and show concrete results. Moreover, multiple manoeuvre detection methods from the literature are applied to this problem, and their accuracy is compared. These include optimal control based methods, symbolic regression methods and reachability analysis.

articleTitle: MLS-net: An efficient convolutional network for multi-scale ship detection in SAR images
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. We proposed a new efficient convolutional neural network (CNN)-based detector with the multi-level supervision (MLS) strategy for multi-scale ship detection in SAR images, referred to as MLS-Net. In MLS-Net, an extremely lightweight backbone network is firstly designed using consecutive residual structures to capture SAR image features in the forward pass. Then, the feature fusion sub-network with three multi-scale feature aggregation modules is introduced to extract high-level semantic features. At last, the MLS-based detection heads are applied on feature maps with different scales to train our CNN in multi-level and then enhance features of multi-scale ship targets in SAR images. Experiments based on the open SAR ship dataset SSDD show that our proposed method achieves the smaller model size and similar detection performance compared with the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Modeling dynamic rural clutter channels with generative adversarial networks
abstract: Time variant rural clutter channels have major effects on radar measurement results or communications, however their amplitude, Doppler and phase characteristics remain difficult to predict. To implement effects of rural bistatic radar channels in a simulated environment, the transfer functions collected from real measurement data in the X-band are analyzed and turned into a reproducible model. A generative adversarial network is proposed to learn the measured clutter transfer function characteristics of a fast fading channel and multiply the dataset of measured clutter channels.

articleTitle: Mutual information-based analysis of recognition of MANPADS missiles
abstract: Studies investigating the recognition of airborne targets usually focus on fighter aircraft and/or commercial aircraft, which tend to be physically large targets with a variety of geometrical features, and associated scattering mechanisms, that can potentially be exploited by a radar for recognition purposes. The focus of this study is the analysis of targets that are physically small and have similar geometrical features. The question is whether the small differences between similar geometries are large enough to allow a radar to recognise these targets. To this end a set of three representative man-portable air-defence systems (MANPADSs) have been chosen for evaluation, namely the Strela, Igla, and Stinger missiles. The significant danger posed by such systems means that their detection and classification is an important real-world problem. This paper makes use of the information-theoretic concept of mutual information (MI) and investigates the comparison of the MI content between simulated monostatic radar cross section (RCS) data for each missile model for VV and HH polarisations. The MI gives a measure of the required signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for classification between the missile types. This MI analysis quantifies the maximum achievable performance for such a system without requiring the design of the full system or the implementation of classification algorithms.

articleTitle: Transfer deep reinforcement learning for accelerated task scheduling in cognitive radar
abstract: Cognitive radars adapt to their environment by continuously sensing, interacting with, and learning from the environment. This paradigm can be applied to a multifunction radar (MFR), which performs multiple functions such as surveillance, tracking, and communications. A radar resource management (RRM) module assigns the necessary resources to these functions according to their priority. While assigning the time resource, RRM becomes especially challenging as: 1) some of the functions (tasks) need to be delayed or even dropped in overload situations, 2) task distributions may change with a changing environment. In this paper, we propose the use of transfer learning (TL) in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) as an effective solution. Our DRL approach is based on Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) aided by a deep neural network (DNN). DNN-based MCTS is slow as it learns from scratch, thereby demanding a large number of rollouts in its search. In changing environments, we investigate how to reduce computational burden using TL. In particular, we tackle the challenge of slow convergence by transferring the policy learned by a DRL agent for a source task distribution to the new DRL agent at a different target task distribution. Our approach shows a remarkable reduction in convergence time compared with its non-accelerated counterpart when tested against different distributions, thereby resulting in a quick adaptation to new environments.

articleTitle: Accurate RCS imaging of car in-cabin objects at sub-THZ frequencies
abstract: Novel efforts to characterize the car-cabin propagation environment at 243 GHz have been made. A Radar Cross-Section (RCS) imaging system is presented for examining the sub-THz scattering properties of individual objects/features found in a typical car cabin. The system is based on Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) techniques, and aims to accurately estimate the spatial distribution of reflection points off objects from various aspect angles. The resulting data aims to increase the knowledge of the relatively complex propagation environment inside a car cabin, and aid development of in-cabin sensing sub-THz radar systems. Presented are measurements made of a steering wheel and a car seat. Individual reflection points could be resolved by a few centimeters using a 10 GHz bandwidth. The front of the steering wheel, which consisted mainly of smooth plastic, produced rather strong specular reflections whilst the fabric car seat produced less intense but diffuse reflections off its center rea.

articleTitle: Influence of covariance matrix mismatch on polarimetric detectors for low-grazing endo-clutter detection
abstract: This paper explores the performances of polarimetric detectors for endo-clutter detections with a ground-based radar in a lowgrazing geometry. We analyse the time series of the covariance matrices of the measured clutter and study the influence of these variations on a benchmark of polarimetric detectors as well as an original detector based on the comparison of the eigenvalues of the clutter polarimetric covariance matrix. Eventually, we predict the performances of each detectors for a given clutter and then assess which class of detector is the best-suited one.

articleTitle: A novel real-time multi-person activity recognition system using millimeter-wave SISO radar data
abstract: Most millimeter-wave radar-based multi-person activity recognition (MPAR) systems are the point cloud-based, which require multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) sensors and cause high cost and power consumption of the systems. To realize an MPAR system using only the single-input-single-output (SISO) radar, a novel recognition algorithm is proposed in this paper, which realizes MPAR through a newly designed SVM classification model based on range and Doppler feature maps. A new feature map synthesis method is proposed for efficient generation of training data and a real-time recognition system is built to evaluate the performance of the algorithms. The experimental results for three scenarios show that the proposed recognition algorithm outperforms the conventional point cloud-based algorithms in terms of average recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Sectorized FMCW radar by modular system design and MIMO sub-arrays for automotive applications
abstract: Automotive radars have evolved in recent years, however, angular resolution and fast processing times demand constant improvements in performance. In this paper, a novel proof-of-concept radar sensor is presented. In particular, a realtime detection approach is proposed which uses a modular radar architecture to achieve a wide field-of-view (FOV). The radar also offers improved angular resolution due to a sparse non-uniform antenna receiver and results are compared to a more standard uniform linear array equivalent. The antennas achieve improved percentage bandwidths in comparison to a more standard microstrip patch antenna solution at the same carrier frequency. In addition, the sub-modular system resolves targets with lower radiation losses in comparison with an equivalent uniform linear array under the same conditions. The proposed radar system is able to achieve a half-power beamwidth of 2.2 degrees using 32 antenna elements arranged in a non-uniform sparse configuration and can detect multiple targets with a range resolution of 10 cm.

articleTitle: Hyperparameters selection analysis of Bayesian deghosting algorithm for MSPSR systems
abstract: In this paper, a recent novel Bayesian deghosting algorithm for the Multi-Static Primary Surveillance Radar (MSPSR) systems is analysed. The previous research was primarily concerned with the verification of the approach based on the Indian Buffet Process (IBP) and its usage as the apriori probability distribution for the bistatic-to-cartesian association matrix. In this paper, the degree of dependence of the algorithm performance on the specific choice of the hyperparameters is explored and assessed. Together with the analysis, the methodology for the choice of hyperparameters without any apriori knowledge is developed. All analyses are verified using simulations derived from a realistic MSPSR system. The results obtained suggest a rather low sensitivity of the association results concerning the hyperparameters computation method.

articleTitle: RD mathematical analysis method for SAR target positioning based on parameter reconstruction
abstract: Target positioning in airborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image is widely used in military and civilian fields. RD positioning model is the most frequently used SAR image positioning model. The traditional iterative method to solve the RD positioning model is complex and has poor stability. In addition, the performance of the positioning results is affected by the accuracy of the airborne motion parameters, and the data output by the navigation system cannot meet the needs of high-precision positioning. Therefore, this paper proposes a SAR target positioning method, which uses mathematical analysis method to solve the RD equations, and reconstructs the airborne motion parameters to reduce the influence of insufficient accuracy, thereby achieving high-precision, fast and stable positioning of target in SAR image. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by experiments results.

articleTitle: Performance of range and velocity estimation in a multistatic radar network with receiver swarms
abstract: This research provides an analysis of the theoretical performance of a multistatic radar system comprised of a single active LFM transmitter and many distributed receivers within a swarm. The Cramér-Rao Lower Bounds on the range and velocity estimation errors of a subset of receivers, including the best performers within the swarm, are used as a performance metric and a Monte-Carlo approach is used to simulate the vignettes containing random distributions of node locations. The performance improvement based on the receiver swarm containment volume and number of receivers within the swarm are presented.

articleTitle: Ego-motion estimation with a lowpower millimeterwave radar on a UAV
abstract: Radar sensors have been shown to be capable of performing simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) tasks. However, single-chip mmWave radar sensors have received little attention because of their limited resolution. In this paper, we present a novel approach to obtain a robust ego-motion estimation of a UAV using a low power single-chip millimeter wave (mmWave) FMCW radar sensor. By using a novel method to match local radar signal descriptors, we are able to achieve a robust trajectory estimation.We then propose to optimise the trajectory by extracting loop closures from low-dimensional latent space descriptors. We validate our solution in an industrial IoT lab with a drone, but it can be applied more broadly in power contrained platforms.

Index Terms: Root Mean Square Error Of Cross-validation

articleTitle: Representation of hypersonic glide vehicles as fluctuating radar targets
abstract: The monostatic RCS of a generic Hypersonic Glide Vehicle (HGV) is presented at S-band and is derived using a Physical Optics (PO) based simulation approach. Target RCS histograms are then produced and used to generate a custom statistical distribution which is subsequently compared against the conventional Swerling models associated with representation of target fluctuation when using the Radar Range Equation (RRE). The accuracy of the Swerling models for this particular target type and frequency band is subsequently discussed.

articleTitle: Radar sparse signal processing by non-negative least-squares estimation
abstract: Increasing the granularity of the solution space for many inverse problems results in ill-posedness. Detection of objects that are close in the solution space e.g. in range or Doppler is significantly improved if a-priori information, such as sparsity, can be used. Alternatively to traditional sparse signal processing algorithms priors, in this paper, we exploit the non-negativity of objects power estimates and propose the use of a non-negative least-squares algorithm to perform single-pulse target estimation. We discuss the corresponding gridding and objects relative-phase effects on estimation as well the relation with other sparse signal processing methods. Finally, we present numerical results supporting that the proposed method, similarly to typical sparsity based algorithms, has the potential to increase detection probability of closely spaced objects.

articleTitle: Clock performance in distributed coherent radars
abstract: Clock phase noise is a limiting factor in the performance of contemporary distributed coherent radio frequency sensing systems such as multi-static radar, constraining the ability to integrate coherently across sensor nodes and over time. Phase noise arises from timing errors introduced by the local oscillator used to generate or mix the RF signals. In multi-static systems, the timing errors at the transmitter and receiver are not self-cancelling as they are in mono-static systems. New clocks with improved stabilities and reduced form factors are emerging from universities and industry, but without simulation it is not possible to know what impact novel timing technologies will have on radar system performance.

articleTitle: Polarization synthesis applied to UHF band SAR data for subsurface object detection
abstract: The detection of buried objects and structures is an important issue for many applications, both in the civil field (non-destructive preventive archaeology) and in the military domain (detection of mines, weapon caches, etc.). Due to its penetration capabilities through the observed medium, radar operating at low frequency is the preferred remote sensing sensor for this type of application. However, due to the relatively low level of reflectivity of targets in this wavelength range, object detection remains a difficult task. Polarization synthesis is a methodology that allows, in an analytical way, to identify optimal polarimetric configurations, in the sense of enhancing the contrast between buried object and the surrounding soil. Applied to experimental airborne SAR data collected in the UHF band during a dedicated flight tests campaign, the polarization synthesis technique has permitted to identify circular polarization (on transmit and on receive) as the most relevant acquisition mode for detecting cylindrical targets of metric dimension buried underground.

articleTitle: Forward-looking imaging for airborne array radar via adaptive sparsity orthogonal matching pursuit
abstract: Forward-looking imaging for airborne radar is of vital importance in remote sensing, independent of daytime and weather. However, the improvement of azimuth resolution for forward-looking imaging is still a challenging problem so far. In the paper, the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm in sparse reconstruction, with the development of adaptive sparsity aiming at blind signal recovery, is proposed to reconstruct the scattering coefficients of targets more accurately corresponding to every single snapshot, and then obtain the final high-resolution forward-looking image via accumulation. Moreover, conventional spatial sampling model is extended to space-time sampling model, equivalent to an increase in the number of measurements, which further improves the azimuth resolution of forward-looking imaging. Finally, both the point and area simulation results are provided to verify the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Bias compensation Kalman filter for 3D angle-only measurements target traking
abstract: Some sensors can only measure the angle of arrival of the signal, but the real position of the signal source is usually interesting. To obtain an accurate target position estimate, this paper studies the target tracking problem based on angle-only measurements in 3-Dimensional (3D) space. Firstly, the target position estimate is obtained by using weighted least-squares (WLS) algorithm, and the covariance matrix of the position estimate is calculated. Although this algorithm has low computational complexity, there is a bias problem due to the transformation of angle measurement equation from nonlinear to linear. To counter the bias, a bias compensation step is considered by estimating the correlation between the measurement matrix and noise vector. The classical Kalman filter (KF) is applied to the target position estimates before and after compensation. In numerical results, the performance advantages of the proposed bias compensation KF over the uncompensated algorithm and extended Kalman filter are verified. In addition, the impacts of angle measurement accuracy and sensor self-positioning accuracy are analyzed, indicating that the bias compensation Kalman filter can achieve high positioning performance with low computational cost.

articleTitle: Simulation and qualitative study of an active antenna array for an aerospace surveillance radar
abstract: An active array is a flexible beamforming technique, which permits to shape the antenna's radiation pattern: steer the main lobe, reduce the sidelobe levels, or generate multiple beams. This paper analyses the effects of power distribution windows on an 8-element active antenna array. The array setting and component block diagram presented objective is to scan the equatorial electrojet from Lima, Peru. Kaiser window is a good candidate since it provides a substantial sidelobe level reduction and maintains a good directivity. Even though, in this scenario, a 0.7 wavelength distance separates the antenna elements, a smaller distance could prevent grating lobes.

articleTitle: Automotive radar image segmentation with frame fusion
abstract: Image segmentation on automotive radar imagery is the key technique for identifying the passable and impassable regions for path planning in autonomous or assistive driving. The availability of consecutive frames which measure the driving scene shifted along with the timeline enables improved segmentation on radar imagery. The frame fusion on automotive radar map is implemented as a two-step procedure: 1) The pixel-to-pixel mapping between consecutive frames is achieved based on an inertial measurement unit (IMU); 2) The information fusion of consecutive frames is achieved based on the Kalman filter. The frame fusion operation leads to correct classification of the initially “unknown” regions and overall improves the confidence of classification compared to single frame segmentation. The segmentation results with frame fusion are presented and compared with the results of single frame segmentation to demonstrate the segmentation improvement.

articleTitle: Log envelope likelihood ratio based velocity filtering track-before-detect method
abstract: Track-before-detect (TBD) method has an advantage in detecting and tracking weak targets, due to the direct use of raw sen- sor data. Velocity filtering based TBD (VF-TBD) is a typical multiframe TBD method, along with the benefit of high energy integration efficiency and well-focused output envelope. However, in conventional VF-TBD methods, the statistical information of raw data is not used for multiframe integration, which may cause performance degradation. In this paper, log envelope like- lihood ratio based VF-TBD is proposed, in which the statistical information of raw data is taken into account adequately for multiframe integration. To deal with the complex and real valued data efficiently, the logarithm of complex envelope likelihood ratio (LCELR) and the logarithm of real envelope likelihood ratio (LRELR) are utilized in multiframe integration of VF-TBD, respectively. The calculations of LCELR and LRELR are presented, and the procedure for multiframe processing of the proposed VF-TBD is provided in detail. Numerical experiments are conducted to compare the proposed methods with conventional TBD methods in terms of computational efficiency, integrated envelope, detection performance and estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Development of a bistatic clutter tool and validation by experimental data
abstract: Clutter seen by bistatic radar systems is typically more complicated than for monostatic systems. Contributions from the illuminator mainlobe to the receiver sidelobe (and vice versa) create clutter returns exceeding typical sidelobe levels seen in monostatic radar. The resulting interference impacts the detectability of targets, and makes accurate clutter modelling critical in the design of bistatic radar systems. We present a bistatic radar clutter model which resolves the clutter gain over a surface grid in Earth-Centred-Earth-Fixed coordinates, allowing real terrain data to be accounted for using digital elevation maps. Results of this model are presented and reviewed. We compare this model to real experimental data collected with two Leonardo experimental radar systems to show that the structure is consistent in this model, for a variety of bistatic and incidence angles.

articleTitle: Counter-OTHR 101: low observability at HF
abstract: Techniques for reducing the HF radar detectability of aircraft, ships and other vehicles have been explored for at least fifty years, but, for a number of reasons, their operational use appears to have been confined to a few niche applications. This situation may now be changing as HF skywave radars are experiencing a resurgence in popularity, so a brief description of some basic countermeasures may be of interest. Here we employ the radar process model framework to associate disruptive measures to the signal physical context as it progresses from waveform generation through to detection, tracking and classification. We then focus attention on the primary issue of target detectability, reviewing the low observable technologies employed at microwave frequencies before examining the extent to which they can be adapted to OTHR. Based on this analysis, we describe two practical methods for achieving a useful degree of echo reduction. To support the theoretical modelling, anechoic chamber measurements of one of these techniques are shown, validating the concept. The paper concludes with some hints as to how a sophisticated OTHR might defeat or at least mitigate low observability techniques.

articleTitle: Characterization of millimeter wave clutter on indian roads at automotive radar frequencies
abstract: Advanced driver assistance systems are increasingly relying on automotive radars for improving road safety. Radar signatures are, however, significantly impacted by road clutter. The characterization of road clutter is vital for optimizing parameters for radar detectors and for generating realistic simulation models of radar data. There has been limited statistical analysis of the road clutter at automotive radar frequencies on Indian roads. In this work, we show that Indian roads are significantly rough, with a roughness of approximately 7mm. The average surface clutter coefficient is −25dB and −23.6dB for concrete and asphalt roads, respectively. The surface clutter coefficient decreases with radar height and grazing angle and varies significantly with temperature. Our study finds that the Gaussian mixture modal (GMM) best fits the clutter statistics.

articleTitle: Multistatic hybrid SAR/ISAR data generation using a stationary target
abstract: There is great interest in multistatic synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems as they are capable of providing high resolution images. These systems could prove promising candidates for provision of surveillance for both military and civilian interest. Both multistatic SAR and its counterpart, multistatic inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR), are limited by their assumptions of observing a stationary target from a moving platform and vice-versa. Hence, without adequate target motion compensation, their resultant radar images appear defocused. Arranging experiments capable of providing repeatable multistatic hybrid SAR/ISAR data of real moving targets can be difficult and costly. One viable approach is the novel method presented in this study, whereby multistatic hybrid SAR/ISAR data can be collected of a target moving with a theoretical motion, without the requirement of an actual moving target – the theoretical motion is brought about through the appropriate motion of antennas. The study demonstrates, both through simulation and experimentation, how radar trajectories of a given SAR system can be altered to arrive at the equivalent setup of observing a moving target. Results from simulation and from an experiment conducted at the Cranfield University Ground-Based SAR (GBSAR) laboratory are presented, showing the utility of this approach.

articleTitle: Application of LV's distribution on the parameter estimation of multicomponent radar emitter signals
abstract: Lv's distribution (LVD) can achieve high resolution while effectively suppressing cross-term and is widely used for signal detection. Aiming at the problem of the detection of multi-component radar emitter signals of a low SNR, a parameter estimation method with weighted LVD is proposed in this paper. The parametric symmetric instantaneous autocorrelation function (PSIAF) of the signal to be estimated is developed first. A scale transformation is then required to decouple the variables. The decoupled PSIAF is followed by a 2D-FFT to obtain the classic LVD result. Then the curve between the LVD results and signal parameters can be fitted. From the curve, we can calculate the weight to correct the power attenuation caused by the limited signal length. Massive simulation experiments show that the proposed method can significantly enhance the robustness of LVD on the premise of maintaining accuracy.

articleTitle: Non-overlapping trajectory multistatic SAR coherent change detection
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Coherent Change Detection (CCD) allows the detection of very small scene changes but is typically reliant on a high degree of similarity in the radar trajectories, with a small baseline. In the case of multistatic SAR imagery, such as those formed by a constellation of SAR satellites, the radar trajectories may have a greater baseline than those collected by a monostatic system such as an aircraft. This paper investigates the effects of multistatic trajectories on the measured coherence between imagery, and how this relates to the spatial frequency (K-space). In particular, the case where radar platform trajectories are greatly dissimilar, but where the K-space image supports still contains a high degree of overlap, is investigated. This paper uses multistatic SAR collections measured at the Ground Based SAR Laboratory at Cranfield University.

articleTitle: Secondary Surveillance Radar replies source separation via the Disjoint Component Analysis
abstract: The foreseen increase of Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) replies, as well the replies emanating from the ADS-B systems will cause many collisions ending into garbling the received replies. While with a traditional receiver the leading reply might be decoded, the trailing ones will suffer a higher failure rate, and the reply will need to be re-issued and lead to an increase of replies density. To combat this and the loss of data, we propose a new mathematical criterion, the Disjoint Component Analysis (DCA), which allows to separate the replies regardless of the SSR protocol, the power ratio or the delay between replies, as demonstrated by several simulations and real data analysis. As we are still missing a computationally efficient algorithmic solution to minimize the cost function of the DCA criterion, this paper mostly demonstrates the potential of said criterion.

articleTitle: Clutter simulation based on WaveGAN
abstract: Abstract—Traditional clutter simulation methods need to establish a fitted distribution model and then to simulate, the generated clutter does not fully match the characteristics of the real clutter due to fitting error and simulation error. And with the improvement of radar resolution, radar clutter shows non-Gaussian and non-stationary characteristics, the existing statistical models can no longer describe the clutter characteristics well. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a radar clutter simulation method based on Generative Adversarial Networks. The one-dimensional voice generation model WaveGAN is applied to radar clutter generation, which simplifies the traditional clutter simulation process, and the generated clutter is better than traditional methods in fidelity. Firstly, the raw clutter data is pre-processed to obtain the training data set; then the original WaveGAN model is modified to obtain a usable radar clutter generation model; finally, Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) is used to quantitatively analyse the distribution difference between the simulated clutter and the real clutter. The result shows that the clutter generated by our method is superior to the traditional clutter simulation method in terms of MMD.

articleTitle: A robust KA-STAP method for terrain clutter suppression in hybrid baseline radar systems
abstract: Suffering from the problem of clutter non-homogeneity, the terrain clutter suppression becomes a significant challenge in hybrid baseline radar system. This paper proposed a robust knowledge aided homogeneous sample selection (KAHSS) method based on an iterative clutter covariance matrix (CCM) mismatch correction processing. First, the initial training samples are selected by prior clutter data that constructed by using the prior knowledge of digital elevation model (DEM). Then, an iterative CCM mismatch correction is performed to select and update the homogeneous samples. Essentially, KAHSS was designed to compensate the estimation bias due to system errors and inaccurate prior knowledge. This allows training samples with similar clutter properties can be selected, and accordingly improves the robustness of CCM estimation. Finally, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can obtain better clutter suppression performance than other contrast methods.

articleTitle: Laboratory multistatic polarimetric 3D SAR
abstract: With the advent of constellations of SAR satellites, and the possibility of swarms of SAR UAV's, there is increased interest in multistatic SAR image formation. This may provide advantages including allowing three-dimensional image formation free of clutter overlay; the coherent combination of bistatic SAR geometries for improved image resolution; the collection of additional scattering information, including polarimetric. The polarimetric collection may provide useful target information, such as its orientation, polarizability or number of interactions with the radar signal; distributed receivers would be more likely to capture any bright specular responses from targets in the scene, making target outlines distinct. Highlight results from multistatic polarimetric SAR experiments at the Cranfield University GBSAR laboratory are presented, illustrating the utility of the approach.

articleTitle: Anti-jamming performance analysis of multi-OAM-mode vortex radar based on waveform diversity
abstract: This paper exploits the electromagnetic vortex (EMV) radar system in anti-jamming applications of digital radio frequency memory (DRFM), considering the orthogonal-waveform-based uniform circular array (UCA) system specifically. Compared to conventional multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) system, the EMV radar has a novel dimension of EMV mode proportional to the orbital angular momentum (OAM), providing a new dimension for the orthogonal decomposition of the transmitted waveform, as well as a new dimension for distinguish the DRFM and a real target.

articleTitle: Trainable complex ISTA variants for radar multitarget detection
abstract: In this work, we implement two complex trainable versions of the well-known iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm (ISTA) method—this is, complex learnable–ISTA (C-LISTA) and complex analytical–LISTA (C-ALISTA)— and apply them on radar signals. We describe how the original algorithms can be modified to handle the complex nature of the signals and discuss the implementation details required for successfully training such models. By means of numerical experiments, we evaluate the performance of the presented methods in terms of probability of detection and benchmark them against the traditional ISTA method. Our simulations show that it is possible to achieve a performance comparable to ISTA but with much lower computational cost, signaling the potential of trainable methods for online sparse reconstruction in computationally demanding surveillance radar tasks.

articleTitle: Cognitive FMCW radar to enhance velocity disambiguation in MIMO systems
abstract: The increments in the chirp repetition interval caused by the utilization of Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) modulation schemes degrades the maximum unambiguous measurable velocity in imaging radars. Commercial FMCW radars constantly deploy Doppler disambiguation methods to every detected target, even if their velocities are not ambiguous, as it is not possible to determine in advance whether the measured velocity is folded or not. In this paper, we propose an online adaptation mechanism to extend the maximum Doppler scale on-demand based on a simple but powerful ambiguity detector, which operates in a triple heterogeneous frame configuration. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first proposal for an online ambiguity detector, which triggers the dynamic configuration of certain phase profiles to reduce the chirp repetition interval and temporary increase the unambiguous Doppler scale. The approach in this paper is aligned with the cognitive radar principles, and does not require a constant execution of disambiguation methods in every frame, which leads to a lower processing overhead.

articleTitle: Preliminary results of UAV ultrawideband SAR tomography based on multi-pass data
abstract: Unmanned-aerial-vehicle(UAV) synthetic aperture radar(SAR) tomography can overcome the overlapping and geometric distortion inherent in two-dimensional(2-D) SAR and provide three-dimensional(3-D) radar images of observation scenes flexibly and cheaply. In 2021, a novel P-band ultra-wide-band(UWB) SAR system was designed and installed on a multi-rotor UAV, and multi-angle multi-pass UAV SAR tomography data was collected using this UWB SAR system. This paper demonstrates a UAV-borne SAR tomography experiment, including system introduction, experiment design, data processing, and imaging results.

articleTitle: Distributed sequential detection based on cell-average CFAR local tests
abstract: In conventional distributed radar target detection, the number of accumulation returns from local sensors is typically fixed and then a decision may be made either when the information accumulated is insufficient or when it is enough excessively. In this paper, we generalize the sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) into distributed detection with local sensors using the cell-average constant false alarm rate (CA-CFAR) tests under unknown noise level. The asymptotic approximated thresholds are calculated in the proposed test. Numerical examples show that the exact error probabilities are closer to the given error probabilities, and the exact expected sample sizes (ESSs) are smaller when using the calculated thresholds than those in Wald's thresholds setting. Performance functions of the proposed method are evaluated through Fredholm integral and numerical results show its superiority compared with Wald's SPRT in performance.

articleTitle: Try living in the real world: the importance of experimental radar systems and data collection trials
abstract: While simulations of increasingly high fidelity are an important tool in radar science, experimentation is still needed as a source of validation for simulation, to explore complex phenomena which cannot be accurately simulated and ultimately in turning theory and simulation into a real world system with real world applications. Experimental systems can range from laboratory based, installations on the ground with limited fields of view all the way up to flying demonstrators which may be prototypes for radar products. In this paper we will discuss the importance of experimentation in the development of radar science and radar products with examples of systems used by a sub-set of the members of the UK EMSIG.

articleTitle: Radar-based indoor navigation system for visually impaired
abstract: The absence of the Global Positioning System (GPS) inside buildings makes indoor navigation more difficult compared to outdoor environments. This paper provides a summary of visually impaired indoor navigation technologies to identify the needs of the visually impaired to safely navigate indoors. Radar as a sensor is preferred because it works in conditions where other systems cannot work properly and has unique features. In particular, this paper reviews different radar SLAM and ego-motion estimation approaches that can aid indoor navigation. This paper concludes with a brief insight into the future direction for a novel radar-based wearable indoor navigation system.
